records.claim: CVE-2023-31290 (GHSA-pm4f-pggw-8jwc) affects Trust Wallet Core before 3.1.1, as used in the Trust Wallet browser extension versions 0.0.172 through 0.0.182; root cause is 32-bit entropy from mt19937 seeded with a single 32-bit value.
records.method: Fetched advisory JSON live from api.github.com on 2026-10-12; saved verbatim at fixtures/source-snapshots/GHSA-pm4f-pggw-8jwc.json
records.notes: Primary source (GitHub Security Advisory). Extension version range 0.0.172–0.0.182 stated in advisory text itself.

records.claim: The vulnerable RNG for the WASM build lived in wasm/src/Random.cpp and constructed a fresh std::mt19937 per call seeded by std::random_device{}() in both random32() and random_buffer().
records.method: Downloaded byte-exact file at that commit via raw.githubusercontent.com; sha256 f8dea1b9bd1e7057a0f7166ef372e3b34fc4a96eb7fa9e31bbd137beb8c5aab1 stored in fixtures/source-snapshots/
records.notes: Direct source verification, not secondary reporting.

records.claim: Fix commit d3c2eee16b154cbb69e8959b01e5e71fbabb1212 ('[emscripten]: use javascript for random generation (#2750)', 2022-11-21) replaced the C++ <random> usage with EM_ASM bridges to crypto.getRandomValues (browser) and Node crypto.randomBytes, failing closed otherwise.
records.locator: commit d3c2eee16b15..., parent 69b2da9826df..., only file changed: wasm/src/Random.cpp
records.method: Commit metadata + diff fetched from GitHub API on 2026-10-12; post-fix file downloaded at same commit (sha256 609bb7543f9d0d1200f7e62c69c428e805b5e2b4600ece2e60656216ae7f096f); local diff of the two snapshots saved as fixtures/patches/d3c2eee16b15.diff
records.notes: Verified files list contains exactly one modified file.

records.claim: The fix commit is tagged as release 3.1.1, matching the advisory's 'before 3.1.1' boundary.
records.locator: tag 3.1.1 -> commit d3c2eee16b15...; tag 3.1.0 -> commit efca5eeef5ab...
records.method: Tag listing retrieved via API pages 1-6 on 2026-10-12; tag->sha mapping recorded in docs/historical-source-analysis.md
records.notes: Note: tags are named without leading 'v' (e.g. '3.1.1'), unlike many repos.

records.claim: wasm/src/Random.cpp was introduced by commit 5b8beb939d08b2b252afff72aeb1388a95d1de19 ('Add Random for wasm (#2240)', 2022-05-24) already containing the mt19937 pattern; content identical through v3.0.0..3.1.0.
records.locator: commit 5b8beb939d08...; verified identical text also at tag 3.0.0 (200bd11232c4...)
records.method: Path history via commits API + raw file fetch at tag 3.0.0 compared visually/by hash
records.notes: Establishes earliest wallet-core version carrying the WASM RNG (file added May 2022).

records.claim: Effective mnemonic entropy of wallets created by the affected extension builds is bounded by ~32 bits (~4.3 billion possible mnemonics), versus 128+ bits expected from BIP-39.
records.locator: random_buffer() fed 16 bytes of entropy to mnemonic generation while each byte stream derives from one 32-bit seed (mt19937 reseeded per call)
records.method: Advisory states it explicitly; our static analysis confirms the per-call reseeding structure; modelling experiment E2 reproduces the state-space collapse mechanism synthetically
records.notes: The exact number of DISTINCT mnemonics reachable depends on how wallet-core consumed random_buffer across multiple calls (per-call reseeding means each 16-byte buffer has ≤2^32 variants; combined multi-buffer entropy is still capped per-buffer at 32 bits). We did NOT rebuild/run the historical WASM binary, so end-to-end mnemonic enumeration count is inferred, not executed.

records.claim: In the vulnerable Emscripten builds, std::random_device was additionally weak/deterministic at runtime (Emscripten historically returned a fixed sequence unless polyfilled), compounding the 32-bit seed bottleneck.
records.source: secondary reports (Ledger blog, community analyses) + Emscripten changelog
records.method: Not directly testable here without building the historical WASM; flagged for further access
records.notes: Plausible and widely reported, but we did not verify the exact toolchain behaviour of the shipped build. The 32-bit mt19937 seed cap holds regardless of random_device quality — that part IS confirmed from source.

records.claim: Exploitation occurred in the wild in December 2022 and March 2023 against extension-created wallets.
records.method: Advisory text; corroborated by Ledger's public post-mortem (listed in references)

records.claim: The patched JS bridge falls back in order: window.crypto/msCrypto getRandomValues → Node require('crypto').randomBytes → throw 'No secure random number generator found'.
records.method: Direct read of post-fix snapshot; logic transcribed and executed under Node.js in experiment E5 (when node available)
records.notes: Fail-closed design verified statically; E5 verifies the transcription runs.

records.claim: random_buffer() in the FIXED version emits one byte per uint32 draw (truncating 24 bits per call) — statistically uniform but wasteful; security comes from the CSPRNG backing, not bit-efficiency.
records.method: Static reading of the loop body
records.notes: Relevant nuance often missed in secondary write-ups.

records.claim: Passing basic statistical uniformity tests does not imply cryptographic security; a 32-bit-seeded MT19937 stream passes chi-square/monobit/correlation checks while having ≤32 bits effective entropy.
records.method: Reproducible run: python -m rng_research.cli run-experiments --experiment E3-modelling-stats-deception
records.notes: Demonstrated on a clearly-labelled MODEL, not on historical binary output.

records.claim: All browser-extension wallets created with versions 0.0.172–0.0.182 during that period must be treated as potentially compromised; users should upgrade AND move funds.
records.method: Advisory text; operational advice outside this lab's scope to verify individually
records.notes: Per-wallet status cannot be determined offline; this is guidance, not a claim we can test.

records.claim: An independent from-scratch MT19937 implementation (init_genrand scalar seeding + twist + tempering) reproduces libstdc++ std::mt19937 output streams bit-for-bit for six uint32 seeds; CPython's seed(int, version=2) contract yields different streams for the same seeds. The lab's Python model is therefore architecture-faithful but NOT proven bit-equivalent to the historical WASM build.
records.source: external oracle: libstdc++ via g++ 12.2.0 (Debian); fetched random.tcc from gcc-mirror tag releases/gcc-13.2.0
records.method: Oracle program compiled and executed locally on 2026-10-13 (Linux/x86_64); outputs recorded with hashes; Python reference engine compared stream-by-stream; difference vs CPython asserted as a regression-guarded test
records.notes: Confirms algorithm-level conformance of the reference engine only. Bit-level equivalence of the MODEL or the reference engine to the shipped Emscripten WASM binary remains UNVERIFIED (see docs/rng-conformance.md, ledger gap L2).

records.claim: A deterministic reconstruction chain (uint32 seed -> libstdc++-convention MT19937 first-outputs low-byte stream -> BIP-39 mnemonic) round-trips exactly and recovers the originating seed in targeted audits; the BIP-39 layer is validated against official test vectors and the MT19937 core against the external g++ oracle.
records.source: this lab's experiments + fixtures/references/bip39_vectors.json (official BIP-39 subset) + mt19937_scalar_vectors.txt (g++ 12.2 oracle)
records.locator: experiment E6-mnemonic-recovery-roundtrip; src/rng_research/mnemonic_recovery.py; tests/test_mnemonic_recovery.py; bip39_vectors.json sha258(over canonical vectors list) 893a88648a421605cda8d0cf15adb153b30bcd4c7ecfd0f70f581a7de491a0ab
records.method: python -m rng_research.cli run-experiments --experiment E6-mnemonic-recovery-roundtrip ; pytest tests/test_mnemonic_recovery.py
records.notes: Confirmed FOR THE MODELLED SEED PATH ONLY. Whether the historical WASM build seeded std::mt19937 with exactly one uint32 via init_genrand remains UNVERIFIED (L1/L2); a recovered candidate seed proves reachability under the model, not historical origin. Enumeration hard-capped at 1,000,000 seeds per invocation by design.
